observations: Recyclable test uses the SIGNED type byte: lea edx,[r15-0x5]; cmp edx,0x3; ja -- type in 5..8 takes the recyclable arm; a type byte >= 0x80 (negative when sign-extended) takes the plain arm and returns sign-extended (0xFFFFFF80 for 0x80). The zero check (or esi,r15d) is also on the signed type, so it only fires for byte 0.

The log_num gate fires before the CRC check: a corrupted log_num byte returns kOldRecord (13) even though the CRC is also wrong (bytes 7..10 are inside the CRC coverage). The CRC coverage of the log_num field is therefore not separately observable through the return code.

The CRC covers header+6 .. header_size+length-6 -- the type byte, the recyclable log_num, and the payload -- but NOT the stored CRC or the length. The stored value is masked; the binary unmasks with (stored - 0xa282ead8) rol 15, the exact inverse of Mask.

The CRC call is the inlined Value -> Extend(0, ...) through a runtime dispatch: the 16-byte thunk at 0x61c25f0 jumps through the .bss slot 0x6508908, which the init stub at 0x61c26d0 fills with ExtendImpl<Slow_CRC32> (0x61c21d0, census-bound). The fast-path check (IsFastCrc32Supported, 0x61c2400) selects the implementation at startup; this packet pins the slow one the slot actually holds.

The decompress loop passes the ORIGINAL length on every Uncompress call (rdx = rbp each iteration) while the input goes null after the first call -- the null-input resume rule from #5972. The loop exits only when remaining == 0 AND produced != kBlockSize, so a full 0x8000-byte output forces another call even with nothing left.

The digest comparison is unreachable by construction: the streamed digest and the recomputed XXH3_64bits cover exactly the appended bytes, so they always agree. The branch is modelled (mismatch -> kBadRecord) and recorded, but no generated case can force it.

buffer_.clear() never writes drop_size on the zero-record and decompress-error paths (only the kBadRecordLen and kBadRecordChecksum paths set *drop_size = buffer_.size() first). ReadMore's own kBadHeader failure is the only way *drop_size is set on the short-buffer path.

Two call sites, one loop: both calls in Reader::ReadRecord set drop_size = 0 and dispatch on the return code through a jump table (cmp eax,0xf; ja). The duplication is a compiler loop-body copy, not two different callers.

Live engine check: pure-Python CRC32C reproduces the standard 0xE3069283 vector for '123456789' and Mask/Unmask round-trip; libxxhash digests the empty input to the known 0x2d06800538d394c2; a real ZSTD frame wrapped in a real WAL record (type 1, correct masked CRC) runs through the model with the real Uncompress shim and returns kFullType with the original payload and fragment_checksum == XXH3_64bits(payload).
